reuse.why: Extends the shared getDateWithSkippedWeekend and adds a shared isHoliday, but the daily skip rule is re-written inline in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange instead of being one shared predicate/helper.

duplication.why: The 'daily && skipWeekend' test and the '!isWeekend && !isHoliday' filter are repeated four times (twice in getNextDate, in getUpcomingDates, in getDatesInRange), along with ad hoc occurrence-window padding heuristics.

placement.why: Holiday matching and the moving loop sit in shared/schedules.ts, but the daily-skip decision is spread across server handlers, and schedule-template still moves daily weekend occurrences via the helper instead of skipping them.

scope.why: Edits stay within the four requested steps (daily skip, new handler, holidays, MM-DD holidays) plus tests; no unrelated edits.

maintainability.why: Fragile take/padding heuristics (count*2+holidays.length, 7+holidays.length, holidays.length+2 days) and four copies of the skip rule make the next calendar-rule change error-prone.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange each filter daily non-working days inline with d.isWeekend || isHoliday instead of going through one shared non-working-day/adjustment helper; schedule-template bypasses the daily rule entirely.

disguised_duplication.where: The same daily skip filter appears as an Array.filter callback in getNextDate (twice) and getUpcomingDates and as an if/continue in getDatesInRange, reshaped rather than shared.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; the daily-skip special case lives outside it at getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange (each reimplementing the non-working check), and schedule-template's two calls never apply the daily rule.
